The Bluetooth connection with the treadmill was lost. The treadmill stops by itself and its session is lost. If the belt keeps moving, press STOP on the console or remove the key.
The treadmill has stopped sending data, so the values on screen may be out of date. If in doubt, press STOP on the console or remove the key.

TreadZ Console needs to find nearby devices and connect to them to talk to your treadmill. It is only used for that.

Without this permission the app cannot find or connect to the treadmill. Android will not ask again: allow \"Nearby devices\" in the app settings.
Notifications are off. Without them the app cannot show its running notice, which also has a STOP button for when the screen is off. Allow notifications in the system settings.

Optional. Shares users, weights and workouts between the devices linked to the same private GitHub repository, and keeps a copy there. Without it everything stays on this device.
Token saved on this device, encrypted. It is never shown again.

On github.com open Settings, Developer settings, Personal access tokens, Fine-grained tokens, and create a token. Under \"Repository access\" choose \"Only select repositories\" and pick your private data repository. Under permissions give \"Contents\" read and write access. Copy the token and paste it here.
The token gives access to several private repositories. Pick the one that holds your TreadZ data.
Nothing has been uploaded yet. If you confirm, this device uploads the records below to %1$s. What is already in the repository is kept and merged: nothing is overwritten.
Cancel uploads nothing and forgets the token.

resources.string: The token is removed from this device and it stops syncing. Your users, weights and workouts stay on this device, and nothing is deleted from the repository. Changes that were not uploaded yet will not be sent.
No connection to GitHub. Your changes are kept and uploaded when the network is back.
GitHub rejected the token. It may be wrong, expired or revoked. Create a new one and paste it again.
The token does not give access to any private repository. Create it with access to your private data repository.
The repository cannot be found with this token. It may have been deleted or renamed, or the access removed.
This token cannot access the linked repository. To use another repository, unlink this device first.
The token can read the repository but not write to it. Give it \"Contents\" read and write permission.
GitHub\'s request limit was reached. It will be tried again later.
GitHub\'s request limit was reached. Try again in about %1$d min.
GitHub is having problems. It will be tried again later.
Other devices were uploading at the same time. It will be tried again.
The repository is too big to be synced.

Create, edit or delete the people who train here. To switch quickly, tap the user at the top of the main screen.

Every two minutes a little faster, finishing strong.
A quick build-up to a long, steady and fairly demanding effort, with small incline changes.

A slow walk on a high incline with small variations.

Repeat a test every 4 to 8 weeks to follow your progress. Differences smaller than about 5 ml/kg/min are within the error of the tests.
A gentle test: about 8 to 10 minutes of walking, first on the flat and then uphill, while the app measures your heart rate. It estimates your VO2max. Needs the chest strap.
A hard walking test: the incline rises every minute until you cannot keep up. It measures your maximum heart rate (it does not give a VO2max).
A hard test: you run at a speed that rises every minute until you cannot keep up. It gives your maximal aerobic speed (MAS), your VO2max and your maximum heart rate.
No valid test yet. Do one to see your VO2max.
You have not done any test yet.
The result is deleted, also on the devices linked through GitHub, and it no longer counts for your fitness figures. The workout stays in your history.
The result could not be saved on this device.
This test is a steady walk of about 8 to 10 minutes, followed by a few minutes of cool-down. Your heart rate is measured the whole time.
This test is a maximal effort. You run at a speed that goes up every minute until you cannot keep up, and it can be very hard. With the warm-up and the cool-down it takes about 15 to 25 minutes.
Do not eat for 2 to 3 hours before.
No hard exercise the day before.
Put the chest strap on: the test needs your heart rate.
You can stop at any time with STOP. The test will then not count.
To end the test, press EXHAUSTED when you cannot keep up. STOP also counts after 3 minutes of increasing speed; STOP before that makes the test invalid.
This is the made-up weight of the generic user. Enter your real weight in the Weight screen.
A comfortable walking pace, between %1$s and %2$s km/h. The speed of your last test is suggested.
The speed of the first stage, between %1$s and %2$s km/h. It then rises 0.5 km/h every minute.
No heart rate yet. Put the chest strap on.

Get ready: the belt is starting.
Walk naturally. The speed may adjust to bring your heart rate into the band, and you can change it too.
Keep walking at this speed. It is fixed now.
Keep walking. The incline is up now: do not hold the handrails.
Keep walking: your heart rate is not steady yet.
Warm up with a brisk walk.
Warm up with an easy jog.
Keep walking. The incline rises every minute: do not hold the handrails. Press EXHAUSTED when you cannot keep up.
Keep running. The speed rises every minute. Press EXHAUSTED when you cannot keep up.
Top speed reached. Hold it as long as you can and press EXHAUSTED.
Walk easily to cool down. The belt stops by itself.
Your MAS if you stop now
Press it when you cannot keep up. The cool-down follows.
Ends the test early and it will not count. You cool down by walking.
During the test only the speed can be changed, and only until it is fixed.
The controls are locked during the test so as not to spoil it. STOP ends it.

The cool-down was cut short. It does not affect the result.

You changed the walking speed before it was fixed.
Your heart rate stayed below the target band even at the fastest walking speed: the result is less certain.
Your heart rate stayed above the target band even at the slowest walking speed: the test cannot be done safely.
The second stage was extended to reach a steady heart rate.

Your heart rate did not change at all: it is not a real measurement.
There was no valid heart rate for several seconds.
Your heart rate went above the safety limit of the test, so it was stopped.
You reached the top speed allowed: your real value is at least this.
You stopped within the first 3 minutes of increasing speed, so there is no meaningful result. The start speed may have been too high.
You stopped before 5 minutes of increasing speed: the effort may not have been maximal.
Your peak heart rate was well below your maximum: the effort may not have been maximal.
Your heart rate stopped rising while the speed kept going up: the effort counts as maximal even though the peak is below your estimated maximum.
The test ended with STOP after at least 3 minutes of increasing speed: it counts as exhaustion, with no cool-down.
There was no usable heart rate: your maximum heart rate was not measured and the effort cannot be judged.
